title: Totally Honest
tagline: We built a confession booth that made a century-old brand feel radically honest.
pullQuote: Everyone has a dental secret. We just gave them a place to confess it — live, on camera, in the Flatiron District.
copy: BCW challenged us to make Colgate’s ‘Totally Honest’ campaign tangible. The insight was simple and uncomfortable: everyone lies to their dentist. Our answer was a custom video booth installed in New York’s Flatiron District, where passersby could step inside and anonymously confess their worst dental habits — on camera. AI face tracking replaced participants’ faces with the iconic Colgate dot while an animated smile mirrored their mouth movements in real time.

The result was something between a confessional and a comedy set — authentic, disarming, and completely on-brand. Content from the activation seeded across digital and social, turning New York’s honesty into Colgate’s most shareable campaign in years.

title: Be Iconic
tagline: We put people inside the future of driving — before the car even existed.
pullQuote: The path you just drove? You drew it. Your signature created the world.
copy: Momentum tapped us to build the centrepiece of Cadillac’s national Lyric roadshow — an immersive experience that would let Canadians feel what it means to drive an electric vehicle that doesn’t exist yet. Using Unreal Engine 5, we rendered stunning real-time environments projected across the Lyric’s windscreen, pulling visitors through cities and landscapes that felt visceral and alive. The experience began with something deceptively simple: signing your name on an iPad.

That signature became the road you travelled — rendered as a glowing path through the virtual world, revealed in a final dramatic pull-back as the journey ended. The message landed without a single line of ad copy: this car isn’t just a vehicle. It’s an extension of you. The roadshow ran at locations across Canada throughout the summer, drawing lines at every stop.

title: Reconnecting New York
tagline: The story of September 12th, told through text messages — exactly as it happened, twenty years later.
pullQuote: In 2001 the most innovative way to communicate was a text message. In 2021 it’s the most personal.
copy: Unit 9 brought us the brief of a lifetime: tell the untold story of the Verizon employees who kept New York connected in the days after September 11th — and tell it in a format nobody had used before. The medium was the message: text messages. We interviewed over 30 Verizon employees from that week, built a precise timeline, and delivered 11 personal stories to participants on September 12th, 2021 — at the exact times the events had occurred twenty years earlier. Each text unlocked immersive phone call reenactments, 360° interactive maps of downtown Manhattan, and AR before-and-after filters of the structural damage to Verizon’s headquarters.

Behind the scenes, we used Twilio-driven SMS to simultaneously push high-volume multimedia content to thousands of participants in real time — a technical challenge that had never been attempted at this scale. The project won the Cannes Gold Lion, One Show Gold Pencil, Clio Gold, and Webby Award.

title: Recent Web Sites
tagline: Fast, stable, and built to last — websites that work as hard as the brands behind them.
pullQuote: The best website is the one nobody notices. They just feel like the brand finally makes sense.
copy: IBC needed a complete rebuild of an architecture that had grown unwieldy from years of constant updates. We restructured their content and rebuilt on StoryBlok headless CMS, making it intuitive for the team to manage and for visitors to navigate. H&R Block’s WordPress site was crashing every tax season under peak traffic load — we moved them to a static generator with CraftCMS, and it hasn’t gone down since. For Karis, a rebrand and repositioning called for a new site that could flex with an evolving identity — we delivered it on StoryBlok with the flexibility they needed.

Three different organizations, three different problems, one consistent principle: the platform should disappear and the brand should speak. These are a few of the sites we’ve built recently that do exactly that.

title: Social Change
tagline: We built an AR app that let incarcerated fathers read their children to sleep.
pullQuote: All the child has to do is point the camera at the page. The rest is magic.
copy: FCB Chicago came to us with something extraordinary: a brief to keep families connected across prison walls. Bedtime Stories is an augmented reality app designed for US inmates — specifically fathers — that lets them read bedtime stories to their children as if they were there in person. A child holds a phone over a printed book page, and their father’s recorded voice fills the room while his presence fills the screen. The technology had to work in the hands of a child, without WiFi, without complexity.

We built it with sixty of the most beloved children’s books in the library, with plans to grow. The response was immediate. The project won the One Show Gold Cube, Cannes Silver Lion, Clio Gold, and ADCC Gold — some of the most decorated work of the year.

title: Poster for Everyone
tagline: A poster that reads the room — and rearranges itself for whoever is standing in front of it.
pullQuote: Accessibility isn’t a feature you add at the end. It’s the whole idea.
copy: TAXI and the Rick Hansen Foundation gave us a challenge with no precedent: build a poster that changes for the person looking at it. Using a Microsoft Kinect sensor, the installation detects the viewer’s height and distance in real time — adjusting font size and layout to accommodate someone in a wheelchair, someone with low vision, or a child. Nobody sees the same poster twice. We also built in ambient language detection: it listens for the language being spoken nearby and changes its display accordingly.

What started as a prototype for an RHF campaign became a proof of concept for a different kind of public communication — one where the message adapts to the audience instead of demanding the audience adapt to the message. The project earned a One Show Merit and a Strategy Magazine Silver.

title: Sweat Machine
tagline: Free Gatorade. But you have to earn it.
pullQuote: The machine knows if you’ve worked for it. Your heart rate doesn’t lie.
copy: TBWA Toronto came to us with the best kind of brief: make people prove they deserve a free Gatorade. We built a custom vending machine equipped with a pulse sensor that measured the user’s heart rate on contact. Heart rate over 120 BPM — clear evidence of real effort — and the machine dispensed a free bottle. Anything less, nothing.

The Sweat Machine turned a product sample into a challenge, and people rose to it. Crowds gathered. People did jumping jacks, sprinted in place, and egged each other on. The video spread fast — because it was exactly what the brand stands for, made physical and immediate.

title: ComplexCon
tagline: We levelled the playing field at the most chaotic sneaker drop on the planet.
pullQuote: At ComplexCon, resellers always won. We built a system that made sure they couldn’t.
copy: Jam3 brought us into one of the most technically complex activations we’d ever built. At ComplexCon, limited sneaker drops are chaos — large-scale resellers scoop product the moment it hits, leaving real collectors empty-handed. Adidas wanted to fix that. We built onto the Complex app, integrating AR, Bluetooth beacons, and a network of internet-connected lockers to create a drop system where every attendee had an equal shot.

Our contribution was the backend engine: a CMS that let Adidas admins schedule and manage drops in real time — controlling locations, inventory, shoe types, and pricing — while processing payments and remotely unlocking the right lockers for the right buyers at the right moment. The system ran without a hitch across a packed convention floor. The project was covered by Engadget and won a Cannes Digital Craft Bronze Lion and two One Show Bronze Pencils.

title: Cadillac XT4
tagline: We turned the car into the controller.
pullQuote: Touch the door. Touch the hood. The car knows.
copy: Isobar and Cadillac wanted to launch the XT4 — a new, fun crossover aimed at a younger buyer — with something that matched the car’s energy. We built an immersive showcase using a wraparound LED screen that filled the viewer’s entire field of vision. Then we turned the car itself into an input device. Using Touch Designer, Microsoft Kinect, and Leap Motion, we mapped touch points across the XT4’s exterior.

Touching the car in key areas — the door, the roof, the hood — triggered real-time interactive animations across the surrounding screens, capturing the excitement and freedom the XT4 was designed to embody. The effect was immediate: the car felt alive before anyone had driven it.

title: Nuit Blanche
tagline: Two and a half weeks to build one of the most ambitious installations of the year.
pullQuote: In beauty, the face is the canvas. We built the studio around it.
copy: Isobar came to us with a project that was equal parts thrilling and terrifying: build a fully immersive, tech-driven installation for Shiseido on the trading floor of the Design Exchange — for Nuit Blanche — in two and a half weeks. Using projection mapping, face tracking, gesture control, and real-time video effects, we created an experience where visitors could interact with Shiseido’s four key product technologies: Dew, Gel, Powder, and Ink.

A Kinect and Leap Motion sensor array let visitors gesture through the space to control two types of projected video and ambient audio simultaneously — their face becoming the canvas, the technology an extension of their creativity. The installation ran for one night and repositioned Shiseido Ginza as a brand that doesn’t just make beauty products. It makes art.

title: Tenor Takeover
tagline: We put live opera singers in a YouTube masthead and let the internet write the lyrics.
pullQuote: The internet submitted bread-related tweets. Professional tenors sang every single one.
copy: Union Creative had an idea that was either brilliant or insane: take over YouTube’s masthead for a day with a live stream of professional opera tenors singing tweets submitted by viewers — in real time, bread-related content only. The technical challenge was significant: simultaneously stream live performers, display incoming tweets, and broadcast everything through a YouTube masthead that had never been used this way before.

The real complexity was invisible to viewers. Every tweet needed legal consent before it could appear — without breaking the flow of the experience. We built a seamless consent and submission interface that kept users inside the moment, and a moderation dashboard that let producers queue tweets for the tenors on the fly. The event ran for one day and won Gold at the Media Innovation Awards and recognition at the Atomic Awards.

title: Chase The Gear
tagline: We turned a Facebook Live stream into a real-life video game with hundreds of players.
pullQuote: What started as a social media experiment became a footrace through High Park.
copy: TBWA had a genuinely unhinged idea for Sport Chek: take a real Olympic hopeful, send them running through High Park, stream it live on Facebook, and challenge viewers to physically show up and catch them to win prizes. We equipped the runners with custom video streaming apps and built proprietary software to push their live feeds directly to Facebook — clean, reliable, and real-time across multiple simultaneous streams.

Nobody predicted how many people would actually show up. Hundreds of participants turned what was meant to be a social experiment into a genuine, chaotic, city-wide event — with runners dodging crowds, fans sprinting through the park, and thousands more watching it unfold on Facebook Live. It won a Clio Bronze and became a case study in how to make a brand genuinely participatory.

title: Go Further
tagline: We turned Ford trucks into playable video games — and kept them running for two full seasons.
pullQuote: The steering wheel is real. The windshield is the screen. The Leafs fans loved it.
copy: Bond Brand Loyalty asked us a question nobody had ever asked before: can you turn a car into a video game? Not a driving simulator — an actual, fully playable game, controlled by the vehicle itself, projected onto the windshield. We said yes. Using a modified steering wheel and accelerometer as input devices, we built a custom Unity game that lived entirely inside the Ford truck, with the windscreen as the display.

The activation ran at Scotiabank Arena for every Toronto Leafs and Raptors home game across two full seasons — a testament to how well it worked. Thousands of fans played it. Nobody had seen anything like it. Bond and Ford kept it going because the lines never stopped.

title: MiO POV
tagline: We let music festival crowds broadcast themselves to the billboards at Dundas Square.
pullQuote: The best way to talk to millennials at a music festival is to put them on a billboard.
copy: TAXI knew exactly where MiO’s audience was: NXNE. The challenge was making a product known for personalization feel personal at scale — to thousands of people at a festival. We built a custom mobile app that let attendees stream their own point-of-view video directly to the giant billboard screens at Dundas Square, live, in real time.

To make it work without festival WiFi killing the stream, we built a private network on-site and installed custom video streaming hardware that handled real-time moderation before anything hit the screens. Every stream was reviewed before going public — without any perceptible delay. The campaign won two Promo Awards Gold and an Atomic Awards Gold.

title: Bachelor Experience
tagline: A virtual bachelor proposed to strangers in malls across Canada. Nobody saw it coming.
pullQuote: Watch the video for the surprise ending.
copy: Launch and CityTV wanted to create a moment for The Bachelor Canada that would escape the screen and live in the real world. We built a large-scale augmented reality installation where a life-sized virtual bachelor — rendered in real time using Unity and Vuforia AR — would appear to propose to unsuspecting mall visitors across Canada.

The technology had to perform flawlessly in unpredictable retail environments: uneven floors, varying lighting, no guaranteed network. We made it work. A viral video capturing the best reactions drove massive reach beyond the installations themselves, connecting CityTV, Media Experts, and Michael Hill in a single activation that was genuinely surprising — the best kind of advertising.

title: Augmented Reality
tagline: Large-scale augmented reality, off a billboard, in downtown Toronto. It had never been done before.
pullQuote: The brief was to do something impossible with AR. We love briefs like that.
copy: Red Urban gave us one of the most technically audacious briefs of our career: build an augmented reality experience that runs off the giant outdoor billboards at Dundas Square, for the launch of the Volkswagen Beetle Turbo. Large-scale outdoor AR — not on a phone screen, not in a controlled environment, but live, at street level, anchored to a massive public display — had never been attempted before.

Using String AR technology, we built an experience that let pedestrians interact with a virtual Beetle through their phones at a scale that stopped people in their tracks. Testing on-site was nearly impossible given the variables — weather, ambient light, distance — but we delivered. The Beetle launch became one of the most memorable outdoor moments in Volkswagen Canada’s recent history.
